quest.title: For a Reunion Without Tears
quest.description: Alice has used her magic to conjure a bubble that recreate your Mondstadt travels so the story can be shared with the knights who have returned from their expedition. As someone who has experienced it firsthand, you gladly agree to test and check it in advance...

chapter.num: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind: Part II
chapter.title: For a Reunion Without Tears

talks.objective: Go to the Knights of Favonius Headquarters and participate in the test

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We made it... Wow, the whole gang's here — even Master Diluc!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Well, Jean wanted my input on everything... Even though I left the Knights, Grand Master Varka has done a lot for me.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: He didn't stop me from leaving back then, or throw any administrative roadblocks my way, so I owe him one.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Well, I was sad to see you go, but your mind was made up... And, anyhow, you're an adult. As long as you're prepared to follow through on your choices, who am I to stop you?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Heh, and lemme tell you, my rebellious streak was way worse back in the day... *yawn*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, you look pretty tired... Late night yesterday?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Yeah, didn't get much sleep at all, and now my head's killing me... All my terrible memories of being Grand Master came rushing back at once.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: The Grand Master's wording is somewhat misleading, so allow me to elaborate.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: We made quick work of our tasks yesterday, much to the Grand Master's great pleasure, so he hit up his friend Charles for a few drinks.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha, you know how it is. When you're catchin' up with an old friend, a few drinks turn into a few too many, am I right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh, so you're just hungover! Ugh, and Paimon was starting to feel bad for you!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I see. Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I just received word from the Knights stationed at the venue that the setup is complete. You can start today's story at any time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I have a question, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Ask away.

choices.text: If everyone can experience the story in the bubble...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Ah, you mean like how only you could have purified Dvalin's tears...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: That ability is unique to you, and to be honest, a lot of people might not even know you're capable of something like that, so they might get stuck at that point in the story.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Don't worry, I thought about that. The story told within the bubble has some jumps. I've deleted the parts that might complicate things.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: The remaining content doesn't require the participant to do much of anything, actually. It should be like watching a play, except you get to walk around as you enjoy the performance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, but we ran into a combat encounter yesterday, when that Fungus jumped out at us...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: We'll take care of that. Alice and I want this to be an experience even a child can complete without trouble.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: The parts you're testing today are more stable, so there shouldn't be too many bugs.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Of course, when you access the dicier sections, be sure to keep our vision in mind.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Understood.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of Alice, where is she?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Klee demanded some playtime with her mom. And, of course, as far as Alice is concerned, nothing is more important than a request from her daughter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, that checks out...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hahaha, well let's get this show on the road. I'm ready to witness our Honorary Knight's story first-hand!

choices.text: There shouldn't be anything in there that only I can do, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew... So this is where the chase ends this time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute! This isn't what their hideout looked like! It's at least a few times bigger!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Yes, I remember it being much more run-down. This place has far more structural appeal.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: The Lawrence Clan lived here for a time, but this doesn't look like their handiwork. And I know for sure it's not the work of the Knights.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Must be a bit of creative license on the part of our dear mages, then.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Alice said the original was too run-down and didn't fit her aesthetic taste.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: So we repurposed some assets from the Golden Apple Archipelago. As you can imagine, Alice has always been a "go big or go home" kind of person.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, this is "go big" alright...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Still, our mission remains the same. We're here to get back the Holy Lyre.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, and this time we have a whole bunch of people to help us, not just Diluc. Should be a total piece of cake!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, dizzy... That's gonna take some getting used to. Why didn't that happen the first time?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ah, looks like we've jumped forward a bit since yesterday... We're at the Favonius Cathedral now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, is this the bit where we st— Or, um, "borrow" the Holy Lyre?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A—And we're sure we wanna expose this little detail?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Paimon's not sure about this... Also, why is Tone-Deaf Bard the only one here? What about Varka and the others?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hehe, don't worry. I'm sure Nicole has it all planned out.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: See, here comes Diluc now.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Word from the Knights of Favonius is that the Fatui are planning to steal the Holy Lyre der Himmel. Unfortunately, that intel came a little late.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: A conflict between the two parties is ensuing inside. If the Fatui succeed, we'll miss our chance to borrow the Lyre.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Come on. Let's go help the Knights.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hm.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: ...What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh, so that's how we're explaining this part. Huh, pretty convincing.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's all thanks to that committed performance from our good friend Diluc.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: I'm just reading the lines Miss Nicole gave me. You need to play along, okay? The Kameras are rolling.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Don't worry. Our operation isn't that strict. If there are slip-ups, I'll just delete them later. Feel free to take a relaxed approach.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, that was Nicole's voice. Where's it coming from...?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Probably... that small bubble.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: That's right. This is a kind of communication magic — the same one the Knights of Favonius used to get in touch with me earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: If you get stuck at any point, you can contact me through this magic, and I'll provide a few hints.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: How very convenient. I suppose, given how the story is progressing, we don't have to worry about "borrowing" the Holy Lyre then.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: That's right. Obviously, we're not including the stealing part in this version of the story.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: After all, the Fatui were the ones who ended up with it. Borrowing, stealing... leaving out that detail doesn't change the direction of the story.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Anyway, the Knights are currently fighting to protect the Holy Lyre. Varka and Jean are already in the underground area. We should head over as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, this is like getting to read the script before watching the movie!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I wonder, what would happen if, this time, we managed to catch the Fatui thief in the act?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: That would... complicate things. Worst case scenario, we might need to do another take, so if you could refrain from going off script, that would be great.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Okay, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Someone's got an axe to grind...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: You're just in time. The situation is not looking good at the moment — the Fatui brought much more force than expected.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's turned into quite a mess.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: You're not bad, boy. Against the Fatui, though... You'll need to try harder than that.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: You ain't messing around, huh? Take this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no. If this keeps up, the Holy Lyre's gonna be—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, sorry. Paimon can't do this. Nicole, shouldn't these people be wearing Fatui costumes at least?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's kinda hard to get in the zone when our opponents look like average guild members.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Huh, let me see here... Ah, it looks like magical auto-load has been disabled, so the Fatui costumes didn't appear.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I'll get that fixed... Just ignore the problem for now and continue with the scene. Remember, this is a tense moment.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Got it. In that case... I'll evacuate the members of the Church right away!

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Alright. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: #As you see, {NICKNAME}... The situation is dire. We need to retrieve the Holy Lyre and get it back to headquarters.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Looks like the Fatui are tied up fighting the Knights. I doubt they have the manpower to spare to deal with us.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Which means, if we rush in, we should be able to retrieve the Lyre.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll see it done.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You all sure are getting into character... Okay then, let's go!

talks.objective: Approach the Holy Lyre der Himmel

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Holy Lyre! There it is!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Well, well, well...

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: It seems our outer diversions were most effective. The Knights know not that the true danger lurks right beneath their nose!

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: It's no wonder you're known as the youngest, most capable Electro Cicin mage in your unit. You can read our enemy like a book.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: No, we're too late!

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Put the Lyre down!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You heard her! Put it down and put 'em up, or this is gonna get ugly!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Wait, why are you the only one with a costume, Fischl?

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Why, because I fashioned this headpiece myself, of course! How does it look? I am the spitting image of an Electro Cicin Mage, am I not?

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: And, I suppose, I look enough like an Electro Cicin as I am.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: ...Hold on. Trying to distract me with conniving conversation, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Hah! You underestimate me, to think I would appear before you without full confidence in my victory! Go forth, Oz— Ahem, Cicins. Take care of these pests.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: The Holy Lyre der Himmel belongs to the Fatui!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Whoa, that was fast — mage-powered flight is something else!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fischl is— Or, um, the Fatuus is getting away! After her, quick!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Here, take it away, and don't let them catch you!

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Hah! That's nothing the gliding champion of the Fatui can't handle!

talks.objective: Track the target to the Fatui hideout

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Alright, here's the crest. And with that, I'm off the clock.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Oh, and by the way, word has it you accomplished something major in Nod-Krai. You reeled in the true moon from beyond the false firmament...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You know about that?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Well, I spend most of my time staring into a scryglass, after all. If something changes in the sky, you think I wouldn't notice?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Hydromancy uses the false stars to reflect true fate within the water. Now, I can't help but wonder what I would we see if I cast a reflection of the true moon instead...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Of course, I need a whole new set of equipment to look into that, which means shelling out a whole lot of Mora. So, I've been taking on a lot of odd jobs.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: No wonder Alice gave you quite a few parts in this.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Generous compensation, minimal manual labor... It's been a good gig. Plus, the Hexenzirkel never promises an amount they can't deliver...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Even though her daughter is, in some part, responsible for my predicament, that was a long time ago, and I know Klee didn't mean it.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Huh, I guess the moon's a big deal in hydromancy. Just spitballing here, but it kinda sounds like your progress would be much faster if you, I don't know... just contacted Barbeloth directly.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Ugh, c'mon! Enough about that old hag. You're doing this on purpose, aren't you?

talks.objective: Track the target to the Fatui hideout

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: A human never doubts what their eyes see, or rejects the ground beneath their feet.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Both now warn you that this is the end of the road. Give up and turn back while you can.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That voice... Is that Mona?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Mona? Oh, you mean Barbeloth's student.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know about her? But, Mona came to Mondstadt after your expedition left...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Well, I had regular contact with the Hexenzirkel, so her name came up now and then. The whole thing about her messing up and being too afraid to go back... Yeah, I know that too.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: WHAT!? But...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: How? No one in the Hexenzirkel should know about that!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: For real? Uh, sorry but I'm pretty sure all the mages know...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: All of them!?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I'm afraid so... Oh, except Rhinedottir, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Fine! That's just... fine. It's not like the old hag's gonna come find me in Mondstadt to settle the score... right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, anyway... How do we cross?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I'm not telling.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Aw, c'mon. Don't take it out on us.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: I'm not! This is... unrelated! Besides, I'm playing a Fatuus whose job it is to issue riddles. You can't just ask me for the answer!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right. Almost forgot about that.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: If you want the answer, think back to what I said at the beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gotta say, Paimon didn't expect you to play this kind of role, Durin...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Well, actually, Aunt Alice was planning for me to play Dvalin if the dragon himself didn't agree to take part. That was the backup plan.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Apparently, there's a spell like the one used to make Simulanka, that could change me back into an evil dragon.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: That does not sound like a good idea.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: I have to agree. That sounds like a disaster waiting to happen.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I don't think I'd be very good at playing the evil dragon, anyway. I'm not intimidating enough...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Luckily, Dvalin agreed to take part after all, so my role was switched to "Timid Fatui Guard B," and I got to wear a costume instead...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that's a pretty huge change. Why "B" though?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Oh, because Mika's "Guard A"...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: As expected, Alice has got it all planned out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like Mika's guarding this spot.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Oh, hey! It's been a while!

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Hello, Grand Master! Hello, everyone—

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: No, wait. My line— Ahem, How did you get in here?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: I would think you have bigger concerns right now. Tell us where to find the Lyre.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: ...It's locked in the back room. But, good luck getting in there. Three crests are needed to enter, and each one is guarded by a Fatuus...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait but, in real life, we only needed one key...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Yes, but there are three locations to visit. If there was only one key to be found, there's a good chance the encounters set up at the other two locations would go to waste.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: All our actors worked so hard to memorize their lines. It would be a shame if their part got skipped over.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Fair point. They're playing through the story just like us, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: To be honest, when I first read my lines, I was kinda confused at how I just... give up the intel without a fight.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: But when I actually had to stand off against all of you... it made sense.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: I mean, Mr. Diluc practically had me in a cold sweat!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Really? I only had one line.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Aha, yet in a game of cards, it's the ones that remain unturned that strike the greatest fear in your opponent. The same principle applies here.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: That's right, and I've been told you have quite a few tricks up your sleeve, Mr. Diluc...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Anyway, you can head in now. Everyone should be ready.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: One moment, we can't quite end it like this. I believe you have one more line, Mika.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Do... *sigh* D—Do I have to say it?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: It would benefit the scene...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Alright. Ahem...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: I—I told you everything I know! Now leave me alone!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And off he goes...

talks.objective: Explore the area and find the crest

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Okay, okay. You win... *sigh* Somehow, this round wasn't quite as fun...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Probably 'cause you had to act like a Fatuus. At this point, I can take down those with my eyes closed haha...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Hahaha, true. Guess I didn't stand a chance, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you were the one in the Fatuus costume! Does that mean the auto-load bug is fixed now, Nicole?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: It would seem so.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Man, their armor is heavy... and not breathable at all. You're telling me the Fatui in Sumeru and Natlan also wear this stuff? I can't even imagine...

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Rumor has it Fatui recruits undergo rigorous training. I feel like there's some truth to that after all.

choices.text: Delusions might also be involved somehow.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Well, even though we lost, Dad had fun for sure! Here's the crest I was guarding. You've earned it!

response.speaker: Cyrus
response.text: Oh, and Bennett told me about what happened in Natlan, how you helped him navigate his past... It's hard to believe we finally have answers after all these years.

response.speaker: Cyrus
response.text: So on behalf of all the adventurers in Mondstadt, truly, I can't thank you enough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that's what friends are for, right?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Speaking of, how have things been since you got back, Bennett?

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Same old same old, hahaha. Bad luck included... But, that part's nothing new, so I don't mind.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: I do miss the Asha though. I hope I get the chance to show them Mondstadt someday.

choices.text: The Harbingers seem like the disciplined ones to me.

talks.objective: Explore the area and find the crest
Explore the area and find the crest

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Dun-dun-dun~

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Dun-dun-dun~

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Da-da-da~

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Da-da-da~

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: This is so fun, Mom!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hehehe, I think so too! Come on, let's blow them aaaalll up!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Mom, when can I play with the magic toy you made me?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Very soon, darling. In fact, it should be ready tomorrow! I just know you're going to love it!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Yay! Can we play together?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Why, of course! We'll have ourselves a splendid time!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: The Fatuus up ahead values wealth above all else. No bargaining chip is off the table.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Luckily, I've prepared a negotiation multitool for this situation. Don't forget to take it with you.

talks.objective: Return to Mika to proceed further

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mika, we have the crests!

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Alright. This elevator's a bit complicated to operate, so Miss Nicole asked me to help activate it. Just one moment...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: No problem. Best of luck up there.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Huh, I don't remember Fatui being this nice. Where's the fun in that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course you wanna make things difficult... C'mon, let's get out of here.

talks.objective: Retrieve the Holy Lyre der Himmel
Retrieve the Holy Lyre der Himmel

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Holy Lyre! There it is! Wait, but Paimon remembers something about a—

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Haha! Hot-blooded, careless, and reckless heroes... Despair, for you have stepped into my trap!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Wait, what? All it did was lock the lyre up?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're surprised by your own trap?

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Well, I wasn't the one who designed it! All Alice said was that activating it would turn the tables!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hah, I see...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: That checks out...

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: (Hmph, they laugh as if they already know what is to transpire... I do not have a good feeling about this.)

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Allow me to clarify before we proceed... How was it that the Lyre was retrieved back then?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: From what I've heard, the Fatui Agent guarding this place was given a thorough beating, and then the lock opened.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: So then... I'm the one who walked into the trap!

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Do not despair, Mein Fräulein. Miss Alice provided us with back-up, did she not? We are not entirely out-matched.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: ...'Tis true. Though thine Prinzessin stands on the cusp of defeat, courage has not yet failed her! Let this be our last stand!

talks.objective: Talk to the Electro Cicin Mage

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: A—A—Alright! I know when I'm beat. You win!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: You were brilliant, Miss Fischl. The recording was fantastic — I'm certain future participants will have a great time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! This role was perfect for you!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Hmph. Your praise is a compliment to your own good sense, yet know that this is but the least of your Prinzessin's abundant talents.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Huh, it doesn't look like the lock has opened, though...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: True. This isn't what we were told would happen.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I doubt the mages want us to just... break it open. It's not their style.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Perhaps we haven't met a certain condition, then?

choices.text: Before, all we had to do was beat up a Fatui Agent...

response.speaker: Fischl
response.text: W—Wait... Does that mean the "beating up" part has to happen for this to proceed? You dare place your Prinzessin in such a scene!? 'Tis an affront of the highest order!

response.speaker: Oz
response.text: I'm afraid it may be the only way to end this, Mein Fräulein. But not to worry — it's all pretend, after all.

response.speaker: Fischl
response.text: ...Very well. I shall allow this trespass, if only to bring this to an end.

response.speaker: Fischl
response.text: Just... be gentle.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're up, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Oh, right. Paimon's the weakest one here. Here goes nothin'.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Ah, it's open.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: *sigh* Miss Alice does love to tease, doesn't she.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Congratulations on obtaining the Holy Lyre der Himmel! That's a wrap for now!

talks.objective: Return to Mondstadt and attend the gathering

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As the performance within the magic bubble comes to an end, the actors return to the real world one after another.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Varka has the Good Hunter staff set up a banquet in front of the Cathedral, inviting all involved to celebrate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, this is quite the gathering! Mmm, and do you smell that? Oh, is that the secret menu Varka was talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like we get to try it out, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's stomach has been rumbling this whole time, so she's gonna dig in. Don't forget to grab some food before it's all gone, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Will do.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Oh, hello. Did you need something?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nope. Just noticed that you seem a lot more relaxed.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: You know, we often threw banquets like this when I was little.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: But then, as more and more of our ranks left on expeditions, and I was left in charge, the number of celebrations decreased. I'm not the most natural entertainer, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Now, seeing a gathering like this after all this time, I can't help but feel a bit... regretful for not keeping up the tradition.

choices.text: Everyone leads in their own way.

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: #Well said, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Barbara?

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: You told me you wanted the expedition members to feel at home.

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: But, in my eyes, the feeling of home isn't something you can force. Home is... what happens when we're all together like this.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: ...You're right. And you know what? I've been coming to the same conclusion.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: The location isn't the most important factor. No matter how far we get from Mondstadt, home is wherever we're together.

choices.text: The return of the expedition force is a good thing...

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: I appreciate the kind words, you two. I will do just that.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: #Make sure to do the same, {NICKNAME}. It's not often you get to make it back here. There's a lot of people waiting to catch up.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Now that we're outside the bubble, and no longer in character, there should be plenty of time.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I will.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hey, Honorary Knight!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Look up!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Pretty stellar view from up here, and the breeze is nice too. Care to join me?

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: *sigh* Of all the places to sit, it just had to be there...?

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: To each their own, I suppose.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: #Just be careful on the way up, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Have a seat. I come bearing drinks. Booze-free, of course. You're welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is quite the spot.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ahhh, well, that's what being home is all about, right? Letting go, feeling at ease... Figure we both deserve that after all this time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mondstadt does feel like home.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: You think so? Heh, glad to hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: There's no place like home... That's what people say, right? The expedition took me far and wide, and still, a little alcohol in my system... it would all come back.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: The Cathedral, this statue, the windmills in the city, the pigeons and dandelions in front of the gate...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: The further away you get, the more you miss it. I might be biased, but... means a lot that you care about this place.

choices.text: This is where things began for me in Teyvat.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #Still, {M#she}{F#he} is more important to me than any specific place.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I get that. The people are what make Mondstadt what it is, too... all the carefree kids running around, livening up the place.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Which reminds me, I never thanked you for helping Mondstadt out back then.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: It takes a special person to do what you did. Most people are helpless in the face of Abyssal corruption. Considering their target was Dvalin... things could have been bad.

choices.text: I don't deserve that much credit.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I suppose Barbatos could have handled it, even though he hadn't been awake for long. But, still... I doubt the ending would have turned out quite so perfect.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Dvalin is family to him, y'know. Having to choose between the dragon's life and Mondstadt's safety... That would've been cruel.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Not to mention, the Wild Hunt would have reached our borders sooner or later. We'd have been stretched thin without your help.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Maybe you've never put two and two together, but what you did in Natlan also helped reduce the threat of the Wild Hunt.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: If Natlan's crisis hadn't been resolved, the two Abyssal powers might have joined forces at some point, making our situation even more dire.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Huh, I guess you're right.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hah, look at us, taking down the Abyss in two separate nations! Doin' the Knights of Favonius proud, aren't we?

choices.text: I feel like Paimon might have a few things to say about that...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hah, I guess not. In any case, for a knight, honor is something you get to define for yourself, no matter what the outside world thinks.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: And that's the question, isn't it? Why do we do what we do? But, I think it's safe to say... You already know the answer.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I do.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Ah, so this is where you've been hiding. Y'know, I don't think this was designed for sitting.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hah, when did you become such a stickler? Come have a drink with us — there's plenty.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Don't mind if I do!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: ...Grape juice? Again?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: You know Charles would never let me hear the end of it if I started drinking without him...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: *sigh* Disappointing, but... understandable.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Oh, I almost forgot. Since this banquet is also for the actors, I invited Dvalin.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hahaha, alright! Might hike up the bill a bit, but who cares? I haven't seen him in too long.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Yeah, well... He turned me down. He never did like being the center of attention...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The city is a little too small for him to spread his wings. Even if no one is afraid of him, he could still take out a windmill or two... Guess it's better not to risk it.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Huh, maybe it's time to draft a proposal to build him a landing pad?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wouldn't that attract even more attention?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #{NICKNAME}'s right. If this is what makes him comfortable, might as well let him be. In the meantime, I propose a toast. To our Honorary Knight!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: To our Honorary Knight!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I often think about our parting at Windrise, you know. And now, almost in the blink of an eye, the final stop on your journey is just around the corner... Snezhnaya.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The Tsaritsa's plans have continued to advance. Now, only the Pyro Gnosis remains free from her grasp.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: But if even The Captain couldn't take Mavuika's Gnosis by force, I guess we don't need to be concerned about its safety for now. So that's good news, at least.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Heh, you wouldn't be taking a dig at someone else's ability to hold onto their Gnosis, now would you, Grand Master?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha, of course not. I'm not one to rub salt in old wounds.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Could've fooled me.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Heh, her Harbingers do often tend to take a rather extreme approach. Just look at Childe or Signora.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But we would be mistaken to ignore the fact that Signora did not win the Geo Gnosis using force.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Right, you told me about the contract Morax signed with her before his death... You're saying she didn't need to resort to violence in Mondstadt either?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: That's right. If she was able to provide a reason convincing enough to persuade Morax, she could have persuaded me no problem.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I suppose she just... didn't think there was a reason to negotiate. I had just woken up, so I must not have seemed like much of a threat.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Honestly, the Gnosis was of no use to me. I didn't care who it belonged to, or what means were used to take it...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I just knew if I fought her in that moment, the Cathedral... Perhaps even the entire city might have become collateral damage.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: True. I wouldn't put it past Signora to take civilians as hostages, either.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So that's the full story...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: In the end, though, it was those same methods that led to her end. After all, her third target — the Raiden Shogun — wasn't a big negotiator back then.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Perhaps Signora's success in Mondstadt and Liyue convinced her that she was a match for the Archon of any nation.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I had to stop her.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: You did the right thing. It pained me to see Inazuma as it was back then. I'm glad things have changed since.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Of course, now the elite force of Harbingers has quite a few missing from its ranks, so I suspect the Tsaritsa no longer has the means to meddle in other nations like she used to.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Who knows? Perhaps a chance to formally meet her in Snezhnaya might come sooner than we think.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Some of our knights remain stationed in Nod-Krai. If you need help, just say the word, and we'll be there.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Heh, the look in your eyes... It's changed a lot since you first set off from Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #But, my advice remains unchanged. Never forget that the journey itself has meaning, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The birds of Teyvat, the songs and the cities, the Tsaritsa, her Fatui and the monsters... they are all part of that journey.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Perhaps earth-shaking truths and indescribable trials await you at the end... Just remember, there is more to life than that.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I will. Thank you.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Alright, that's more than enough acting like a real Archon for one night...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: And still, not a sip of drink for dear old Venti at a time like this...? You're no fun, Varka!

choices.text: I'm getting closer to the truth. I can feel it.
My title's just "honorary," remember? Not quite sure the Knights can take credit for Natlan.
I didn't even know I could do that until that moment.
#This is where I began my search for {M#her}{F#him}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, Mona? Again?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: What, the more roles you play, the more you get paid. That's what Alice said. I was hoping to do even more than this, but it is what it is... Anyway, ahem...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: The crest is with me. All I need to know is... how much you're willing to cough up to get it.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Let's talk business, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Heh, looks like we were followed. Guess Mondstadt's elite aren't to be underestimated, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Stand aside. This one's personal.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: But this time, I'm fully locked and loaded! Come on, kid, let's finish what we started!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: The Fatuus up ahead values wealth above all else. No bargaining chip is off the table.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: What? They handed over their crests?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...Looks like the decision has been made for me, then. Further resistance would be foolish.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Coming here first? Hm, I'd reconsider if I were you.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: You've been warned. Continue at your own risk.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Hah! Not a chance. If that's your offer, might as well call it here.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Hmm... No. We both know this crest is worth more than that.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Good enough for me. Gotta know when to fold, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Hehehe, who would've thought there was this much Mora to be made in a dump like Mondstadt...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, did you just break character?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: What? Of course not!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Heh, that's all? You have to at least make it worth my while.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Talk about bad luck... The minute you put on that Fatui costume, the gun stopped working. Hahaha... How weird is that?

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Heh, yeah. Thanks for stepping in, Dad. Guess I'll have to hand it in to Miss Nicole for repairs later...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Ugh, c'mon! Enough about that old hag. You're doing this on purpose, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I'm just glad I didn't have to play the evil dragon in the end...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Without the crests, I can't activate this device either... Like I said, I told you everything I know. Just leave me alone.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Man, I thought I lucked out with just a few lines, but it still wasn't easy to pull off.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Anyway, if you want to get into that room, you'll need to track down the three Fatui with the crests.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I doubt you need a hint for this area. Go on now — the underground chamber awaits!

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: What a coincidence... Or perhaps I should say, great minds think alike.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes, well... This looked like the most relaxed part of the performance.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I'd prefer to get this over with and return to my work as soon as possible. I'm assuming you feel the same, Miss Lisa?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Of course. After all, this place suffers from a dire lack of comfortable chairs and good tea.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: *panting* I couldn't keep up with you after all, Grand Master... It's like you've gotten even stronger since I last saw you.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Expeditions have a way of doing that to people. Ever consider taking your adventurers out on a long trip?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Hahaha, I think I'll pass.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: I never thought I'd get the chance to spar with the Cavalry Captain...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Hehe, I'm always up for a duel, as long as you treat me to a glass of wine after we're done.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Best of luck up there.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: If the conflict really had escalated to this point back then... *sigh* Just imagine the cleanup work.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Yeah, good thing it didn't turn out like that. No use thinking about something that didn't happen, right?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: ...When your free time is as precious as mine, it's hard not to think about it.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Mona's riddle was as follows: "A human never doubts what their eyes see, or rejects the ground beneath their feet."

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: However, things that are taken to be indisputable are often false. So, one must shift one's gaze elsewhere. Perhaps... upward.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: The Fatuus up ahead is courageous and loyal. Be prepared for a head-on clash.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: The Fatuus up ahead is a pragmatist. You might have a chance to avoid conflict if you obtain the other crests first.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Wanna eat at our table? A whole bunch of friends are there!

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Alright. Let the relaxing begin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry! Paimon'll save you a serving of every delicious dish!

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Noelle! I've been looking everywhere for you. Come on, join us!

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Just give me one second. I need to bring a few crates of drinks over first. But I'll be done soon, I promise!

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Haha, in that case, I'll help you out!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: ...As the battle hung in the balance, I spoke an incantation from the Immernachtreich, broke through their ranks with ease, and thus the Holy Lyre was mine! Hmph, 'twas light work for one such as I.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Cyrus told me all about it. You were amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Having seen it for myself, I must admit... You were quite something, my lady. Why, I bet even Barbatos himself would have been hard pressed to catch up with you!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: (That was Hexenzirkel magic not some incantation, but... Whatever. Guess I'll let her have her moment...)

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Even though I didn't have a lot of lines, I still had fun. It... kind of felt like being back in Simulanka.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Acting out a light-hearted script alongside a bunch of friends... It was nice to have a laid-back experience for once.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Quite a change of pace from our experience in Nod-Krai, huh.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Yeah, this was far less complicated.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Haha, you can say that again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice! We made it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The road ahead is almost completely blocked. Looks like this person isn't taking visitors.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess we'll just have to be careful. We need that crest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, we got all the crests. Let's head back and look for Mika.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Security's tight around here.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I hope this is safe...
